title: Financial Crime and Compliance Conferences Fall 2026: The Complete Calendar
summary: Eight financial crime, compliance and fintech conferences in fall 2026. Dates, cost, audience, date conflicts and which deserves your travel budget.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Eight major financial crime, compliance and fintech conferences run between early September and mid-November 2026, and two pairs of them collide on the same dates. Given that global spending on AML and know-your-customer compliance runs to roughly $304 billion a year according to research by Ronald F. Pol, and that PwC's[EMEA AML Survey 2026](https://www.pwc.lu/en/financial-crime/anti-money-laundering/emea-aml-survey-2026.html) found a third of institutions expect costs to rise a further 10-30%, the choice of which two or three events to attend is a real budget decision. This calendar covers dates, cost, audience and what each event is genuinely good for.


## The full calendar


Every event below is US-based apart from the November GASA summit in Bangkok. Cost bands are approximate and reflect what organizers publish; where pricing is not publicly listed, that is noted rather than guessed.


Event Dates City Primary audience Cost band Best for


Global Anti-Scam Summit America Sep 2-3 San Francisco Cross-sector: banks, telecom, platforms, enforcement, NGOs $299-$1,499; virtual free Scams, APP fraud and mule networks


Stablecon Sep 9-11 National Harbor, MD Issuers, banks and payment firms; 1,000+ C-suite Not publicly listed GENIUS Act readiness and stablecoin settlement


FinovateFall Sep 9-11 New York Bank, credit union and fintech executives; 2 in 3 are executives Tiered; free senior places available Rapid vendor evaluation via live demos


XLoD Global New York Sep 24 New York 650+ non-financial-risk executives at large institutions Not publicly listed Three lines operating model and control transformation


Sibos Sep 28-Oct 1 Miami Beach 10,000+ from 160+ countries; banks and market infrastructure Roughly EUR 275-3,400 Correspondent banking, cross-border and market infrastructure


ACAMS The Assembly Sep 29-Oct 1 Las Vegas BSA officers, AML and sanctions leads, regulators, law enforcement Member and early-bird discounts; hybrid option Supervisory expectations and 15 ACAMS credits


Money20/20 USA Oct 18-21 Las Vegas Payments and fintech; roughly 1 in 3 C-suite ~$3,599 rising to ~$4,199 Partnerships, deals and commercial decisions


Global Anti-Scam Summit Asia Nov 10-11 Bangkok Cross-sector, Asia-Pacific focus Tiered by sector Regional scam networks and cross-border enforcement


## The calendar conflicts worth knowing about


Two collisions matter when planning. Stablecon and FinovateFall run on identical dates, September 9-11, one in Maryland and one in New York. An institution interested in both stablecoin settlement and compliance tooling has to split a team or pick one.


Sibos and the ACAMS Assembly also overlap almost entirely — September 28 to October 1 in Miami Beach against September 29 to October 1 in Las Vegas. These serve genuinely different audiences, so the conflict is less painful, but a global bank sending both a correspondent banking lead and a BSA officer will be running two trips in the same week on opposite coasts.


The wider pattern is that the entire season compresses into five weeks. Four of the eight events fall between September 24 and October 1. Teams that plan in August get their pick; teams that plan in September are choosing from what is left.


## What each event is actually for


### Global Anti-Scam Summit America — September 2-3, San Francisco


The distinguishing feature is that this is not a banking conference. Telecom risk teams, platform trust and safety staff, law enforcement and victim-support NGOs sit alongside bank fraud leads, and the programme covers the parts of the scam lifecycle that happen before money moves. Ticket pricing is tiered by sector from $299 to $1,499, with free virtual attendance. Read the[full Global Anti-Scam Summit America 2026 guide](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/global-anti-scam-summit-america-2026-guide) .


### Stablecon — September 9-11, National Harbor, Maryland


Marketed as a Washington DC event and physically in Maryland, which catches travellers out. The 2026 edition lands in an awkward regulatory moment: all seven federal regulators missed the GENIUS Act's July 2026 rulemaking deadline, yet the law still takes effect on the earlier of January 18, 2027 or 120 days after final rules. Issuers are building against proposals. See the[Stablecon 2026 guide](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/stablecon-2026-guide) .


### FinovateFall — September 9-11, New York


Built around 70-plus live seven-minute demos with slide decks banned, which compresses weeks of vendor calls into an afternoon. Risk and compliance is one of four 2026 innovation pillars. Community bank and credit union executives get restricted Spotlight sessions, and qualifying senior staff at financial institutions can attend free through the Leadership program. See the[FinovateFall 2026 guide](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/finovatefall-2026-guide) .


### XLoD Global New York — September 24, New York


A single dense day for 650-plus non-financial-risk executives at systemically important institutions, organised explicitly around the three lines of defence. The format is debate and pre-booked roundtables rather than presentations, and the organizers' own thesis is that the three lines model is buckling under control-testing fatigue. See the[XLoD Global New York 2026 guide](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/xlod-global-new-york-2026-guide) .


### Sibos — September 28 to October 1, Miami Beach


Swift's[annual event](https://www.swift.com/events-training/sibos) , in Miami for the first time, under the theme "Digital finance for AI-driven economies." More than 10,000 attendees from over 160 countries and 100-plus exhibiting financial institutions make it the most international event on the calendar. For financial crime professionals the relevance is correspondent banking, cross-border payment transparency and market infrastructure rather than domestic examination work. Passes range roughly from EUR 275 to EUR 3,400, and visa invitation letters are available — worth starting several months early for attendees who need one.


### ACAMS The Assembly — September 29 to October 1, Las Vegas


The densest anti-financial-crime programme in the US, with 140-plus speakers across roughly 78 sessions, a 2026 theme of "Insight vs. Noise," and 15 ACAMS credits. The federal Regulatory Roundtable is the single most valuable hour available to a practitioner all season. Networking is self-directed, with no hosted-buyer or meeting-matching platform. See the[ACAMS Assembly Las Vegas 2026 guide](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/acams-assembly-las-vegas-2026-guide) .


### Money20/20 USA — October 18-21, Las Vegas


The largest and most expensive event on the list, and a commercial one. Four content pillars cover borderless architecture, agentic AI, partnerships and regulatory guardrails. The value comes from meetings booked through SmartMeet rather than from sessions. See the[Money20/20 USA 2026 guide](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/money2020-usa-2026-guide) .


### Global Anti-Scam Summit Asia — November 10-11, Bangkok


The third GASA regional summit of 2026, following Europe in June and America in September. Relevant for institutions with Asia-Pacific exposure, where a large share of industrialised scam operations are based.


## Which one deserves your travel budget


Most teams can justify two events, and many only one. The honest answer depends less on seniority than on what the role is accountable for.


**A community bank or credit union BSA officer** should go to the ACAMS Assembly and nothing else. The community banking track exists, the peer group operates at comparable scale with comparable examiner expectations, the 15 credits count toward continuing education, and federal officials are on the programme. FinovateFall is a reasonable second choice if the institution is actively buying technology, particularly given the restricted Community Bank Spotlight and the free senior passes. Money20/20 is a poor use of a limited budget at this profile — the pass alone costs more than an ACAMS trip in total.


**A fintech compliance lead** has the hardest choice, because the answer splits on remit. If the job is examination readiness, monitoring quality and regulatory interpretation, ACAMS delivers more. If the job includes banking partnerships, product launches and vendor selection, Money20/20 or FinovateFall put the counterparties in the room. FinovateFall is the better value of the two and the demo format suits early-stage evaluation; Money20/20 is worth its price only when there is a specific commercial objective attached.


**A large-bank Chief Compliance Officer** should look at XLoD Global first. It is the only event where the peer group is narrow enough that benchmarking on control counts, testing ratios and operating models produces comparable answers, and the single-day format costs little time. Pair it with the ACAMS Regulatory Roundtable if the calendar allows, and send someone else to the fintech events.


**A crypto or stablecoin compliance lead** should go to Stablecon. The GENIUS Act's compliance stack — a risk-based AML programme, customer identification, monitoring calibrated to on-chain flows, sanctions screening against wallet addresses — has to be operational before the law takes effect, and the issuer community working through the same problem is concentrated in one place. Money20/20's Borderless Financial Architecture pillar covers similar ground from the payments side if budget allows both. Groundwork on[building a crypto AML programme](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-build-a-crypto-aml-compliance-program) makes either trip more productive.


**An internal auditor** should go to XLoD Global, which is the only event on this calendar with a dedicated third-line stream and sessions on building a future-fit internal audit function. ACAMS carries financial crime audit content as part of a much broader programme, which is a reasonable alternative for auditors whose remit is specifically AML.


**A fraud or scams lead** should go to the Global Anti-Scam Summit. It is the only event where the telecom carrying the initial message and the platform hosting the fake advertisement are in the room, and interventions upstream of the payment are cheaper than anything downstream. Practitioners working on the convergence of these functions may find[fraud and AML convergence](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/what-is-framl-fraud-aml-convergence) a useful frame beforehand.


**A correspondent banking or global payments lead** should go to Sibos, which has no real substitute for cross-border and market infrastructure work.


## How to evaluate vendors on any of these floors


Every event on this calendar has an exhibit hall, and the same six questions cut through all of them. They are worth carrying on a phone.


The final question does the most work. Conference floors are dominated by platforms validated at the largest institutions, and a reference at comparable scale settles fit faster than any capability matrix. Teams doing this systematically often find it easier to shortlist beforehand from a survey of[AML software options](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/best-aml-software) and treat the floor as a way to test claims rather than discover vendors.


Sphinx works on top of the systems an institution already runs, automating the analyst work that follows an alert while keeping every decision documented and reviewable.


## Making the season worth the money


Three habits separate teams that get a return from these events from teams that get a stack of business cards.


Set the objective before booking, not after arriving. "Shortlist two vendors for alert triage," "get a read on examiner expectations for AI-assisted decisioning," or "find three peers who will discuss control testing ratios" are objectives. "Stay current" is not, and it produces nothing an expense review can defend.


Book the constrained formats early. Roundtables at XLoD, SmartMeet slots at Money20/20, ConnectMe meetings at FinovateFall, Spotlight sessions for community banks and credit unions, and the complimentary CAMS seminar at ACAMS all have capacity limits, and they are where the value concentrates. The open-access sessions will still be there.


Write up findings within 48 hours and name an owner. Supervisory signals and peer benchmarks decay fast in memory, and a short memo naming one specific gap and one specific person occasionally produces a change. Conference notes that stay in a notebook never do. For teams whose main constraint turns out to be volume rather than process,[closing the AML efficiency gap](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-close-the-aml-efficiency-gap) is usually the more productive place to start than another tool.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are the major financial crime and compliance conferences in fall 2026?


Eight events run between September and November: the Global Anti-Scam Summit America (Sep 2-3, San Francisco), Stablecon (Sep 9-11, National Harbor MD), FinovateFall (Sep 9-11, New York), XLoD Global New York (Sep 24, New York), Sibos (Sep 28-Oct 1, Miami Beach), ACAMS The Assembly (Sep 29-Oct 1, Las Vegas), Money20/20 USA (Oct 18-21, Las Vegas) and the Global Anti-Scam Summit Asia (Nov 10-11, Bangkok).


### Which conference is best for an AML or BSA officer?


ACAMS The Assembly in Las Vegas. It carries 15 ACAMS credits, runs a federal Regulatory Roundtable with senior officials, includes dedicated community banking, sanctions and digital assets tracks, and draws practitioners across institution sizes rather than only the largest banks. It is also available as a hybrid event, so a colleague can cover parallel tracks virtually.


### Which fall 2026 conferences overlap?


Two pairs collide. Stablecon and FinovateFall both run September 9-11, in Maryland and New York respectively. Sibos (September 28 to October 1, Miami Beach) overlaps almost entirely with the ACAMS Assembly (September 29 to October 1, Las Vegas). Four of the eight events fall between September 24 and October 1, so the season compresses sharply in late September.


### Which conference is best for stablecoin and crypto compliance?


Stablecon, held near Washington DC for proximity to policymakers. The GENIUS Act treats permitted payment stablecoin issuers as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act, and the law takes effect on the earlier of January 18, 2027 or 120 days after regulators finalize implementing rules — which had not happened as of the statutory July 2026 deadline. Money20/20's Borderless Financial Architecture pillar and the ACAMS digital assets track cover adjacent ground.


### How much do these conferences cost?


The range is wide. The Global Anti-Scam Summit prices by sector from $299 to $1,499 with free virtual attendance, and Sibos runs roughly EUR 275 to EUR 3,400. Money20/20 USA is the most expensive at around $3,599 rising toward $4,199. ACAMS and FinovateFall use tiered pricing with member, early-bird and complimentary senior options, and FinovateFall offers free places to qualifying directors and above at financial institutions. Stablecon and XLoD Global do not list pricing publicly, so both require contacting the organizer.
